gallery.title: File:US Airmen aboard CH-53, during Mayagüez incident 1975.jpg
gallery.credit: U.S. Air Force photo 090424-F-1234P-027 from the National Museum of the U.S. Air Force
gallery.source: US Airmen aboard CH-53, during Mayagüez incident 1975
gallery.description: U.S. Air Force security policemen assigned to the 56th Special Operations Wing, Nakhon Phanom Royal Thai Air Force Base, Thailand, aboard a Sikorsky CH-53C Super Jolly Green Giant (s/n 68-10933, callsign "Knife 13") of the 21st Special Operations Squadron. The crew of five and the 18 passengers airmen died when the helicopter crashed 64 km west of the airfield on 14 May 1975 due to a mechanical malfunction, about one hour after this photo was taken. A main rotor blade separated from head in flight.

gallery.filename: Gig of USS Henry B. Wilson (DDG-7) rescues USAF personnel off Koh Tang island on 15 May 1975.jpg
gallery.title: File:Gig of USS Henry B. Wilson (DDG-7) rescues USAF personnel off Koh Tang island on 15 May 1975.jpg
gallery.description: The gig of the U.S. Navy guided missile destroyer USS Henry B. Wilson (DDG-7) rescues U.S. Air Force personnel on 15 May 1975. The gig rescued crews of two USAF helicopters shot down in the attempt to rescue the SS Mayaguez and her crew that had been seized by Cambodian Khmer Rouge on 12 May.

gallery.description: View of the wreck of a U.S. Air Force Sikorsky CH-53C on the beach of Koh Tang island, Cambodia, on 15 May 1975, during the Mayaguez incident. At left is a burning Cambodian patrol boat hit by shells from the U.S. Navy guided missile destroyer USS Henry B. Wilson (DDG-7).

gallery.filename: Four U.S. Navy A-7E Corsair II attack Koh Tang island, Cambodia, on 15 May 1975.jpg
gallery.title: File:Four U.S. Navy A-7E Corsair II attack Koh Tang island, Cambodia, on 15 May 1975.jpg
gallery.description: U.S. Navy Ling-Temco-Vought A-7E Corsair II of Attack Carrier Air Wing 15 (CVW-15) attack Koh Tang island, Cambodia, on 15 May 1975, during the Mayaguez incident. CVW-15 was assigned to the aircraft carrier USS Coral Sea (CVA-43) for a deployment to the Western Pacific from 5 December 1974 to 2 July 1975.
